archetype.name: Dual-Threat (veteran backup)
archetype.definition: A 12th-year insurance quarterback who wins short and on the move, with legs that have ranked among the position's better rushing totals for most of his career, now asked mainly to keep the offense on schedule when Jayden Daniels can't.

report.headline: Efficient in cameo duty, but the shine sits in garbage time and tiny samples
report.take:
Mariota is Washington's QB2, and his 2026 is three appearances long: relief work in a Week 2 loss at Dallas, every snap of a 33-31 win over Seattle in Week 3, and a Week 4 start against Indianapolis that ended after four throws with the MCL sprain he is still listed Questionable for. Daniels started Weeks 5 and 6. Read everything below through that lens: 57 dropbacks is a scouting report, not a season.

On those dropbacks the profile is clean. He has thrown it short and on time, 30 attempts in the 0-9 yard range at 0.389 EPA with a 8.9 CPOE, and he has not turned it over, with no interceptions and no lost fumbles. His aggressiveness is down 4.9 points from last year, and his interceptions are down from 0.78 a game to none, so the trade is coherent: fewer tight-window shots, no giveaways. The 0.21 EPA per dropback ranks 10th of 45, and his 7.8% TD rate ranks 3rd.

The numbers hide where that efficiency came from. His 12 dropbacks while trailing by nine or more added 7.2 EPA, more than the 5.4 his dropbacks added in total, and in one-score games he sits at -0.014 EPA per play, roughly a league-average passer. Third downs have been rough at -0.276 EPA with a 26.7% conversion rate, and throws of 10+ air yards are completing at 33.3%, papered over by three touchdowns. The 14.3% pressure-to-sack rate, 2nd of 38, runs against his whole career. He has usually sat near the bottom of the league there, including 36.5% in 2018 and 37.8% in 2022, so it should drift back toward his norm as the sample grows.

Going forward, his ceiling is set by Daniels' health more than by anything Mariota does. And whenever he plays, he loses his most productive target: Terry McLaurin, at 0.419 EPA per target on 13 looks, is out for the season with a torn patellar tendon. If Mariota is pressed into starts, expect the career version: a mobile, short-area operator good for roughly league-average efficiency, with the 2026 polish fading.

strengths.title: Short-area timing and accuracy
strengths.body: Throws under 10 air yards have been the engine: a 77.8% completion rate and 0.248 EPA across 36 attempts, with the 0-9 band carrying an 8.9 CPOE. That fits a career CPOE that has ranked 13th in both 2018 and 2025, so the accuracy on quick throws is a real trait. The exact EPA rate on these throws will cool, but the skill holds.

strengths.title: Ball security in a conservative shell
strengths.body: He has no interceptions and no turnover-worthy fumbles, and his aggressiveness is down 4.9 points from 2025. This is a choice to live underneath, and it suits a backup whose job is to avoid losing games. Zero interceptions won't last, since he has thrown at least seven in every full-ish season, but a lower rate than last year is plausible given the approach.

strengths.title: Legs as a designed-run threat
strengths.body: His two designed runs averaged 22 yards, including a 35-yard day in a 16%-snap start, and he has posted top-13 rushing yardage in most of his career seasons. Two carries is nothing statistically, but the rushing dimension is long-established and keeps defenses honest when he plays.

concerns.title: Efficiency inflated by trailing game script
concerns.body: The 12 dropbacks while down nine-plus added 7.2 EPA. In one-score situations, 42 plays, he is at -0.014 EPA per play with a 38.1% success rate. Soft coverage and loose defenses when a team is behind tend to flatter backups, so his 'real' level is closer to average than to the 10th-ranked mark.

concerns.title: Pressure is constant, and sack luck should fade
concerns.body: He has been pressured on 38.9% of dropbacks, the worst rate of 38 qualifiers, behind a line whose hit rate allowed ranks 27th. Only 14.3% of pressures became sacks this year, against a career that routinely ranked in the bottom handful there. Expect that to regress, and with it more drive-killers like the third-down struggles already showing.

concerns.title: Losing McLaurin removes his best outlet
concerns.body: McLaurin produced 0.419 EPA per target and accounted for 5.4 of Mariota's target EPA. He is now out for the year. Diggs, at 0.072 EPA per target, and the rest of the room have done much less with Mariota, and Dyami Brown has been a hole at -0.987. This is a structural downgrade, not noise.

trend.note: He went from a 45%-snap relief outing (6.7 EPA) to a full game against a top defense (3 TDs, 3.8 EPA) to a 16%-snap start cut short by the knee sprain. Since then Daniels has reclaimed the job, so there is no meaningful trajectory, only fragments.

nextGame.headline: Plush matchup on paper, but he's QB2 on a sprained knee
nextGame.body:
If Mariota sees the field against Philadelphia, the setup is kind. The Eagles rank last in both hit rate and sack rate, which directly eases the pressure problem that has dogged him. Their pass defense ranks 27th in EPA, and WR1s have feasted at 0.54 EPA a play, 28th. That shifts the spotlight to Diggs now that McLaurin is gone. Washington is a 4.5-point favorite with a 40.5 total, which points to a controlled, run-leaning script rather than the catch-up throwing that padded his numbers.

The real issue is availability and role. He is Questionable with an MCL sprain, the coach says he's on track to practice this week, and he is listed QB2 behind Daniels, who started the last two games. Unless Daniels is hurt, his projected line is a clipboard. On the other side, Philadelphia is missing edge Nolan Smith Jr. and corners Michael Carter II and Jakorian Bennett, thinning an already weak pass defense. They are also without Lane Johnson, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks on offense, which makes a Washington lead and fewer dropbacks more likely.

keyMatchups.title: Leaky line meets nonexistent pass rush
keyMatchups.body: Mariota has faced pressure more often than any qualifier, but Philadelphia generates hits and sacks less often than anyone. With Nolan Smith Jr. out, that gap widens. If he plays, this is the one week his pocket should be clean.

keyMatchups.title: Diggs against a WR1-friendly secondary
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia has let lead receivers produce 4 PPR points a game over their averages and 0.54 EPA per target. With McLaurin done, Diggs inherits that role, though his 0.072 EPA per target with Mariota leaves room to grow.

keyMatchups.title: Low total, favored script
keyMatchups.body: A 40.5 total with Washington laying 4.5 suggests a game managed on the ground against a 31st-ranked run defense. That cuts into the trailing-game volume that built most of his passing EPA.

nextGame.watch: Whether he's a full practice participant and still listed behind Daniels. That decides whether any of this matchup matters to him.

restOfSeason.body:
As long as Daniels is healthy, Mariota is a zero most weeks. The useful forecast is what he looks like in a spot start. Expect a version closer to his 2025 than to his 2026 cameos: short, accurate throws, some designed runs, and roughly league-average efficiency. The garbage-time cushion, the zero-interception line and the elite pressure-to-sack rate are the parts likely to regress.

Losing McLaurin lowers the ceiling, and the offensive line's pressure rate is a lasting problem rather than a blip. In a start I'd project something like 170-230 passing yards with one to two touchdowns and modest rushing, about what his 113 yards a game would look like stretched to full-time volume.
